title: The ineligible selected-cell scan stops at the event that settles the verdict, removing 64% of an ineligible one-cell read
decision: retained, implemented in litchi-ooxml-common and litchi-xlsx
code_state: two additive public items in litchi-ooxml-common (mce::ActiveFlow, mce::process_markup_compatibility_stream_with_stoppable_observers); one crate-internal helper and one scanner return type in litchi-xlsx; no breaking change, no new unsafe, no new dependency, no weakened limit
reason_codes: decision 8 of change 0652 authorizes the movement of the timing of error returns for an ineligible XLSX read and asks for the -63% change 0597 priced, measured on the landed change

0597's frozen candidate was not landed: a bounded memmem pre-gate skips the prefix as well as the tail, so it loses refusals the stream reaches before the verdict is decided, and decision 8 authorizes moving where a refusal is raised, not removing one

stopping at the marking event instead keeps every byte before the verdict under exactly today's parsing and validation, removes more work than the pre-gate on both fixtures, and applies to all nine ineligibility reasons rather than only a <cols> in the first 8 KiB
the verdict is monotone: Scanner::mark keeps the first reason and Scanner::finish returns it without consulting other state, so no event after the first mark could change the published outcome
the whole-corpus transcript is byte-identical on both legs, including every value, every typed refusal, every logical read and every logical byte
every worksheet part in the corpus is ineligible, so the gate governs every source-backed selected read of this repository's fixtures

accepted_evidence.instructions: callgrind isolation pairs N=1 and N=11 differenced and divided by 10, two fixtures, both legs, inclusive annotations at --threshold=99.99
accepted_evidence.corpus_differential: 180 .xlsx packages, up to three sheets each, twelve addresses and two ranges per sheet, a fresh SourceBackedWorkbook over a counting positional source for every read; 4,606 read rows plus 180 catalog lines per leg; the two transcripts are byte-identical
accepted_evidence.verdict_census: the first three worksheet parts of every package (326 parts) read through raw::selected_worksheet::scan over a counting BufRead, both legs: verdict, bytes pulled, part size
accepted_evidence.first_error_matrix: 60 synthetic packages in the 0541 style, generated by change 0597's script retargeted, read at 15 coordinates through the public SourceWorksheet::cell and cells; 900 rows per leg; 210 moved rows over 15 packages, with the complete witness list retained
accepted_evidence.mutation_set: one worksheet per NotEligibleReason variant, all nine, each with a long inert tail: verdict, bytes consumed by both scan and scan_range, and the materialized parser's exact answer, pinned by test
accepted_evidence.timing: 30 samples per leg of 20 reads each, 5 warmup samples, order A1 B1 B2 A2 plus F1..F4 for the A/A floor, CPU 13, for the two ineligible fixtures through the retained probe; and the harness's three selected-cell and range cases in the same order and window as the eligible controls

accepted_costs.refusal_identity: a worksheet that is both ineligible and malformed after its mark now reports the materialized parser's typed refusal instead of the stream's; eight distinct witnesses over the 60-package matrix, tabulated in the record with before and after text
accepted_costs.one_acceptance: one of those witnesses (before-cols__prefix-bad-entity, both shapes) turns a refusal into an acceptance, because the malformed entity sits in a child of the element that marks the worksheet; the materialized parser accepts the same bytes and accepted them before this change, so litchi_xlsx::Workbook::open already returned a value for that package
accepted_costs.stream_bounds: max_event_bytes and the attribute, context-byte and depth bounds now apply only up to the marking event; max_input_bytes and max_output_bytes are the part's declared size and are independently enforced by ZIP member verification
accepted_costs.removed_post_mark_checks: the post-mark <dimension> and <mergeCells> placement questions the scanner asked from state frozen at the mark are removed as unreachable; the materialized parser answers them, with the identical message for the merge family and a more accurate one for the dimension family
accepted_costs.instruction_counts: instructions rank work, not latency; callgrind counts rep movsb per byte and runs SHA-256 in software, which is why the paired timing is reported beside them and only as corroboration

known_gaps.matrix_exhaustiveness: the 60-package matrix is the oracle for refusal identity; it is not claimed to be exhaustive over all malformed worksheet inputs
known_gaps.limit_ceilings: whether the stream's per-event bounds and the materialized parser's own bounds coincide for every part shape is still not established; this narrows change 0597's open question (a) rather than closing it
known_gaps.eligible_corpus: every worksheet part in this repository's corpus is ineligible, so the eligible path is covered by unit tests and the harness's generated corpora, not by a real-corpus eligible differential
known_gaps.edit_routes: the source-backed edit routes and the eager Workbook route were not differenced; the changed code is reachable only from raw::selected_worksheet
known_gaps.timing_floor: the real fixture's A/A p50 floor is 8.12%, above the 5% threshold, so the magnitude of the timing improvement rests on the instruction counts
known_gaps.peak_rss: no allocation, RSS, cold-cache or physical-I/O measurement was taken

withheld: any registered speedup, throughput, cold-cache, physical-I/O, allocation, peak-RSS or concurrency result
any claim that the first-error matrix exhausts the malformed-input space
